target.name: probe-plan
target.source_summary: agents/tester.md + schemas/probe-plan.schema.json + the coverage requirements moved out of the release-gate authorship

gates.description: The probe plan matches its schema: every probe has id, tier, method, path, expect.status, critical_area, and a source_ref with quote/source/line.

No critical area is both probed and declared unprobeable; every unprobeable area carries a reason; every probe carries a non-empty source_ref quote+source (in the pipeline the quote must also resolve against the real source docs).

dimensions.description: Every critical area with a surface in scope is probed, or explicitly listed unprobeable with a reason.

anchors.1: Only the happy path probed; auth, error, and limit behaviors with surfaces in scope are silently absent — no unprobeable declaration either.
anchors.3: Main areas probed, but at least one in-scope critical area (e.g. a 401 path, a 429-with-context, tenant isolation) is neither probed nor declared unprobeable.
anchors.5: Every in-scope critical area — auth (401/403), error responses (the Level-4 shape on at least one path), limit enforcement (429), state/tenant isolation when profiled — is probed or unprobeable-with-reason.

dimensions.description: Each probe's source_ref quotes a real line from the vision/spec — the plan of proof traces to declared intent, not invented behavior.

anchors.1: source_refs are fabricated, generic, or quote nothing that appears in the source documents.
anchors.3: Most probes trace to real source lines; at least one quotes intent that the source documents do not actually state.
anchors.5: Every probe quotes an actual line of the vision/spec that motivates it; a reader can follow probe → quote → source line.

dimensions.description: Probes assert specific, falsifiable expectations — status plus body/header shape where it matters — not just a 200.

anchors.1: Probes assert only a status code, or 'returns something', for behaviors whose body shape is the actual contract.
anchors.3: Status codes precise, but at least one error-shape or auth-body contract is asserted only by status.
anchors.5: Each probe asserts the status and, where the contract is the payload (error body fields, auth cookie, usage numbers), the specific body/header shape.

aggregation.gate_handling: Apply gate caps after normalization; lowest applicable cap wins.

weight_rationale: coverage is heaviest because an unprobed critical area becomes a not_executed status the synthesized gate fails closed on — a coverage gap is a release blocker by construction, so the plan of proof is where it must be caught.

unmeasurable_rules.rule: source_ref quotes resolve against the real source docs
unmeasurable_rules.home: checks/checks.mjs :: source_refs_resolve (deterministic, run in the pipeline probe-plan gate-set)

known_good.summary: Login-feature probe plan: happy, auth, error-shape, health; billing unprobeable.
known_good.content: Probes: [P1 e2e GET /health expect 200 body_includes 'ok' — deployment_correctness — source_ref{quote:'/health returns 200', source:'spec.md', line:14}; P2 api POST /login expect 401 body_includes 'nextSteps' — auth — source_ref{quote:'invalid credentials return 401 with actionable body', source:'spec.md', line:22}; P3 api POST /login (over limit) expect 429 body_includes 'resetDate' — error_responses — source_ref{quote:'usage limit returns 429 with usage/limit/reset/upgrade', source:'spec.md', line:31}]. Unprobeable: [billing — 'no billing surface in this scope']. Every probe asserts status plus the body field that is the actual contract.

known_bad.summary: Happy-path-only plan: one 200 probe, no auth/error coverage, no source_refs, no unprobeable list.
known_bad.content: Probes: [P1 e2e GET /health expect 200 — deployment_correctness — source_ref{quote:'', source:'', line:0}]. Unprobeable: []. Auth (the spec's 401/403 paths) and the 429-with-context error shape are neither probed nor declared unprobeable; the single probe asserts only a status; the source_ref quotes nothing.
